newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan civilians say expelled from Taleban town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan civilians say expelled from Taleban town.

text.p: Thousands of Afghan civilians fled their homes in a town north of Kabul on Tuesday, saying the Taleban militia who recently recaptured the town had ordered them to leave, witnesses said.

"Through loudspeakers, the Taleban ordered civilians to leave Charikar and we started packing and collecting whatever we could carry," Ustad Shgasi, a primary school teacher, told Reuters at the Khair Khana pass leading into the capital.
Thousands of civilians were seen trekking towards the city, carrying their belongings on trucks, trailers or handcarts, their children wrapped in blankets against the bitter cold.

No immediate comment was available from leaders of the Islamic Taleban militia, who have said they are determined to disarm civilians in the town of Charikar and other villages captured in an offensive north of Kabul last week.

The Taleban seized Charikar, about 50 km (31 miles) north of the capital, and the nearby Bagram military airbase on Thursday in a lightning offensive against forces loyal to General Abdul Rashid Dostum and Ahmad Shah Masood.
The Taleban captured the same territory soon after seizing Kabul in September but lost it after Masood, military commander in the ousted government, hit back with guerrilla tactics.
